es.summary: Disminución de la velocidad y amplitud del movimiento, característica principal de la enfermedad de Parkinson. Se manifiesta como dificultad para iniciar la marcha, levantar de una silla y expresión facial escasa.
key_points: Es el síntoma motor más distintivo de la enfermedad de Parkinson.
Puede progresar a akinesia (ausencia total de movimiento).
Se asocia con rigidez muscular y temblor de reposo.
El tratamiento incluye fármacos dopaminérgicos y estimulación cerebral profunda.
Afecta la capacidad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria.

pathophysiology: Degeneración de neuronas dopaminérgicas en la sustancia negra.
Disminución de dopamina en los ganglios basales altera la vía motora directa.
Se produce exceso de actividad inhibitoria, ralentizando la iniciación del movimiento.
risk_factors: Historia familiar de enfermedad de Parkinson.
Exposición a pesticidas o metales pesados.
signs_symptoms: Dificultad para iniciar la marcha o levantarse de una silla.
Rigidez muscular y temblor de reposo pueden coexistir.
diagnostics: Evaluación clínica con escala UPDRS; puntuación alta en ítem de bradicinesia.
Imagen cerebral (MRI) para descartar otras causas, pero suele ser normal.
Respuesta positiva a levodopa confirma diagnóstico.
treatment: Levodopa/Carbidopa – aumenta la disponibilidad de dopamina.
Estimulación cerebral profunda (DBS) en casos refractarios.
complications: Caídas por lentitud y pérdida de equilibrio.
Desarrollo de akinesia y rigidez severa.
nursing_care: Evaluar capacidad de iniciar movimiento y nivel de independencia en ADL.
Monitorear respuesta a medicación (mejora de velocidad de marcha).
Implementar medidas de seguridad para prevenir caídas.
Fomentar ejercicios de estiramiento y marcha asistida.
patient_teaching: Tomar levodopa con alimentos ligeros y a la misma hora cada día.
Informar sobre efectos secundarios como náuseas o hipotensión ortostática.
Practicar técnicas de inicio de marcha (paso pequeño, usar apoyos).
Mantener actividad física regular para preservar movilidad.

outcomes: Movilidad: caminar 50 m sin asistencia en 2 semanas
Autocuidado: realizar higiene personal sin ayuda en 1 semana

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de independencia en cada actividad de la vida diaria y registrar limitaciones
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar áreas específicas donde la bradicinesia afecta la función.

interventions.action: Programar sesiones de fisioterapia para ejercicios de iniciación de movimiento y marcha asistida
interventions.rationale: Mejora la velocidad y la confianza al caminar.

interventions.action: Administrar levodopa según prescripción y observar respuesta motora
interventions.rationale: Optimiza la disponibilidad de dopamina y reduce la bradicinesia.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de uso de bastón o andador
interventions.rationale: Proporciona apoyo físico y disminuye el esfuerzo al iniciar el movimiento.

interventions.action: Planificar descansos programados durante actividades prolongadas
interventions.rationale: Previene la fatiga que exacerba la intolerancia a la actividad.

outcomes: Seguridad: sin caídas durante la hospitalización
Integridad cutánea: piel intacta sin lesiones por caídas

interventions.action: Evaluar riesgo de caída usando escala de Morse al ingreso
interventions.rationale: Identifica pacientes con mayor probabilidad de lesión.

interventions.action: Mantener el entorno libre de obstáculos y asegurar buena iluminación
interventions.rationale: Reduce factores ambientales que provocan caídas.

interventions.action: Colocar barra de apoyo y asiento firme al lado de la cama
interventions.rationale: Facilita el levantamiento seguro y previene caídas al iniciar movimiento.

interventions.action: Instruir al paciente a solicitar ayuda antes de levantarse o caminar
interventions.rationale: Promueve la seguridad y evita intentos de movimiento sin apoyo.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de hipotensión ortostática después de la medicación
interventions.rationale: Previene desmayos que pueden causar lesiones.

en.summary: Decreased speed and amplitude of movement, the primary hallmark of Parkinson’s disease. It presents as difficulty starting gait, rising from a chair, and reduced facial expression.
key_points: It is the most distinctive motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease.
It can progress to akinesia (complete absence of movement).
It is associated with muscular rigidity and resting tremor.
Treatment includes dopaminergic medications and deep brain stimulation.
It affects the ability to perform activities of daily living.

pathophysiology: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra.
Reduced dopamine in the basal ganglia disrupts the direct motor pathway.
Excess inhibitory activity slows initiation of movement.
risk_factors: Exposure to pesticides or heavy metals.
signs_symptoms: Difficulty initiating gait or rising from a chair.
Muscular rigidity and resting tremor may coexist.
diagnostics: Clinical evaluation with the UPDRS scale; high score on the bradykinesia item.
Brain imaging (MRI) to rule out other causes, usually normal.
Positive response to levodopa confirms diagnosis.
treatment: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) in refractory cases.
complications: Falls due to slowness and loss of balance.
Development of severe akinesia and rigidity.
nursing_care: Assess ability to initiate movement and level of independence in ADLs.
Monitor medication response (improvement in gait speed).
Implement safety measures to prevent falls.
Encourage stretching and assisted walking exercises.
patient_teaching: Take levodopa with light meals at the same time each day.
Inform about side effects such as nausea or orthostatic hypotension.
Practice gait initiation techniques (small step, use supports).
Maintain regular physical activity to preserve mobility.

outcomes: Mobility: walk 50 m without assistance in 2 weeks
Self‑care: perform personal hygiene without help in 1 week

interventions.action: Assess level of independence in each activity of daily living and record limitations
interventions.rationale: Identifies specific areas where bradykinesia affects function.

interventions.action: Schedule physiotherapy sessions for movement initiation and assisted walking exercises
interventions.rationale: Improves walking speed and confidence.

interventions.action: Administer levodopa per prescription and observe motor response
interventions.rationale: Optimizes dopamine availability and reduces bradykinesia.

interventions.action: Teach the patient techniques for using a cane or walker
interventions.rationale: Provides physical support and reduces effort to initiate movement.

interventions.action: Plan scheduled rest breaks during prolonged activities
interventions.rationale: Prevents fatigue that exacerbates activity intolerance.

outcomes: Skin integrity: intact skin without fall‑related lesions

interventions.action: Assess fall risk using the Morse scale upon admission
interventions.rationale: Identifies patients with higher likelihood of injury.

interventions.action: Keep the environment free of obstacles and ensure good lighting
interventions.rationale: Reduces environmental factors that cause falls.

interventions.action: Place a grab bar and firm chair beside the bed
interventions.rationale: Facilitates safe rising and prevents falls when initiating movement.

interventions.action: Instruct the patient to request help before standing or walking
interventions.rationale: Promotes safety and avoids attempts at unsupported movement.

interventions.action: Monitor for orthostatic hypotension after medication
interventions.rationale: Prevents fainting that can cause injury.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to Parkinson’s Disease

summary.1.quote: Clients with PD have difficulties initiating movement, such as walking or getting up out of a chair.

key_points.1.quote: Bradykinesia may progress to akinesia, which is the inability to move.

key_points.2.quote: Rigidity: Rigidity involves stiffness—the resistance to movement by both flexors and extensors.

key_points.4.quote: occupational therapy to teach clients how to use adapted tools and methods to make activities of daily living easier

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurologic condition that destroys some of the dopamine-secreting neurons of the substantia nigra, a critical area of the brain that produces dopamine and has an important role in controlling an individual’s movements.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Their writing becomes small and cramped, which is referred to as micrographia .

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Clients with PD have difficulties initiating movement, such as walking or getting up out of a chair.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Also, clients usually present with an expressionless face or flat affect due to facial rigidity.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: The four primary motor manifestations of overt PD (shown in Figure 11.3 ) are (Capriotti, 2020; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, 2023b): Tremors: This involuntary quivering is progressive and often begins in one isolated area, such as the head or hands, and then often spreads to the legs.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Brain scans to rule out other disorders (Note that computed tomography [CT] and magnetic resonance imaging [MRI] scans of people with PD usually appear unremarkable.)

sections.complications.0.quote: The result is impaired balance and increased risk of falls.

sections.complications.1.quote: Bradykinesia may progress to akinesia, which is the inability to move.

sections.complications.2.quote: The loss of NE may explain several nonmotor manifestations seen in PD, including: Mood changes, such as depression and anxiety Cognitive changes, such as memory loss, impaired judgment, poor decision-making, and dementia
